reason: While the text contains three named characters—Job (אִיּוֹב), God/YHWH (יְהוָה), and Satan (הַשָּׂטָן)—not all of them can accurately be characterized as 'leaders.' Job is described as 'great among all the people of the East,' making him a prominent figure of authority. God is clearly the supreme authority. However, Satan is portrayed as an accuser or prosecutor in the heavenly court (the role he plays in disputing with God), rather than as a leader in the conventional sense. Additionally, the narrative includes significant unnamed characters—Job's children and servants—who are featured in the plot and play roles in the events described, further complicating the claim that only named characters appear in the text.
